MCCS Camp Pendleton operates 12 fitness facilities across the installation—including Paige Field House (Mainside) and area fitness centers in the 14, 21, 22, 31, 33, 41, 43, 52, 53, and 62 Areas, as well as MCAS—that offer a wide range of programs, training modalities, and wellness services for Marines, Sailors, and authorized patrons. 

### 1. Human Performance & Wellness Services
Located primarily at **Paige Field House (Bldg 1110, 13th Street)** and **Camp Horno (53 Area)**, the Human Performance program offers free services to all authorized patrons (by appointment):
* **Assessments & Testing:** Body Composition and Bone Mineral Density Analysis (via DXA machine), Resting Metabolic Rate (RMR) testing, VO2 Max fitness assessments, body fat testing, cholesterol screenings, and blood pressure assessments.
* **Nutrition & Health Counseling:** One-on-one nutrition counseling, *Nutrition 101* classes, *Nutrition and Fitness for BCP* (Body Composition Program), and tobacco cessation counseling.
* **Warrior Network Group:** Courses designed to equip Marines and Sailors with mental and social fitness skills to improve resilience and readiness.
* **Contact to Schedule:** Call Paige Field House at (760) 763-3793, Camp Horno at (760) 763-0419, or email `penhumanperformance@usmc-mccs.org`.

### 2. Warrior Athlete Readiness & Resilience (WARR) / HITT
* **Combat-Focused Conditioning:** Semper Fit’s High Intensity Tactical Training (HITT) and WARR programs provide comprehensive, combat-focused strength and conditioning designed to enhance operational fitness and reduce preventable injuries.
* **Dedicated HITT Areas:** All Camp Pendleton fitness centers are equipped with specialized HITT areas, equipment, and certified staff.
* **Unit PT & Force Fitness Instructor (FFI) Support:** Certified strength and conditioning coaches are available to lead specialized unit combat training classes, and quarterly symposiums are held to support FFIs and WARR-certified Marines.

### 3. Group Exercise (Group X)
* Group X classes are offered to enhance overall physical fitness, mobility, and cardiovascular health. 
* For the current class schedule or more information, call the Paige Field House Group Exercise line at (760) 763-0657 or the main Paige Field House desk at (760) 725-6394.

### 4. Massage Services
* Professionally certified massage therapists offer **Deep Tissue, Hot Stone, Swedish, and Therapeutic** massages (with special discounts available during the week of your birthday).
* **Locations:** Available at the 14 Area Fitness Center (Bldg 14013), 22 Area Fitness Center (Bldg 22160), and MCAS Fitness Center (Bldg 2369).
* **Contact:** Call (760) 725-6288 to inquire about pricing and book an appointment.

### 5. Races, Athletics & Alternative PT
* **Hard Corps Race Series:** Hosts major base-wide races and family fitness events throughout the year, including the *Marine Corps Mud Run*, *Heartbreak Ridge Run*, *Shamrock Stampede*, *Run to the Radar*, and *Zero Dark Dirty Obstacle Night Run*.
* **Intramural & Adult Sports:** The Athletics Department runs fee-based 8-week Adult Sports Leagues (open to active duty, dependents, retirees, and DoD civilians 18+) as well as the free *Commanding General’s Cup* competitive tournaments for active-duty personnel. For sports inquiries, call (760) 763-0453 or email `cpenathletics@usmc-mccs.org`.
* **Alternative Unit PT (Outdoor Adventures):** Active-duty units can schedule free alternative PT sessions—including surf lessons, stand-up paddleboarding, mountain biking, hiking, and archery—by calling (760) 421-4938 or emailing `pen.oa@usmc-mccs.org`.

### 6. Facility Amenities & 24/7 Unmanned Access
* **24/7 Access:** All 12 Camp Pendleton fitness centers offer 24/7 unmanned access for authorized patrons (18 years and older) with a registered Common Access Card (CAC). Prior registration at a fitness center during staffed hours is required.
* **Family Fitness:** A dedicated Family Fitness area is available at Paige Field House (Bldg 1110).

turns.agent:
**MCCS** stands for **Marine Corps Community Services**. 

It is a comprehensive set of programs, products, and services designed to support and enhance the operational readiness, warfighting capabilities, and overall quality of life for active-duty Marines, their families, retirees, and civilian employees across the Marine Corps. 

Operating at over 2,250 facilities worldwide, MCCS serves as a single portal for support throughout a Marine's entire career and affiliation with the United States Marine Corps.

### What MCCS Does
MCCS delivers a wide variety of quality-of-life programs and amenities, which generally fall into the following categories:

*   **Marine & Family Programs:** 
    *   **Child and Youth Programs:** Child Development Centers (CDCs), youth sports, and teen activities.
    *   **Family Readiness:** Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB), deployment support, and the Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP).
    *   **Personal & Professional Development:** Education assistance, transition readiness (TRS), family member employment assistance, and personal financial management.
    *   **Prevention & Counseling:** Behavioral health support, counseling services, substance abuse prevention, and victim advocacy.
*   **Semper Fit & Recreation:** 
    *   Fitness centers, intramural sports, and high-intensity tactical training (HITT).
    *   Outdoor recreation, equipment rentals, camping, marinas, and golf courses.
    *   The **Single Marine Program (SMP)**, which focuses on quality-of-life initiatives, recreation, and community involvement for single and unaccompanied service members.
*   **Retail, Dining, & Services (Business Operations):** 
    *   Shopping through the **Marine Corps Exchange (MCX)** and specialty retail stores.
    *   On-base dining, clubs, bowling centers, movie theaters, and entertainment.
    *   Lodging (Inns of the Corps), automotive services, and barber shops.

### Next Steps
If you are looking for specific programs, facility hours, or contact information, please let me know which Marine Corps installation you are interested in (such as **Camp Pendleton**, **Camp Lejeune**, **Quantico**, **Okinawa**, or **MCAS Miramar**), and I can provide tailored details for your base!

The **Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP)** is a mandatory Department of Defense enrollment program for active-duty service members who have a dependent (spouse, child, or dependent parent) with a diagnosed physical, intellectual, developmental, or emotional condition requiring specialized medical or educational services. 

The program is designed to support military families before, during, and after Permanent Change of Station (PCS) relocations through two main functions:
* **Assignment Coordination:** Ensures your family member's medical and educational needs are considered during the assignment process so you are stationed in areas where appropriate care and resources are available.

### 1. Reduced-Cost IVF Nearby (Naval Medical Center San Diego)
Although TRICARE does not cover IVF directly, the Department of Defense offers ART services (including IVF) at a **greatly reduced cost** on a first-come, first-served basis at eight military hospitals nationwide that host OB/GYN Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility (REI) graduate medical education programs. 

Fortunately, **Naval Medical Center San Diego (Balboa)**—located just south of Camp Pendleton—is one of those eight facilities. 
* **How it works:** Their Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility clinic offers ovulation induction, IUI, and IVF. Patients undergoing IVF receive treatment both at NMCSD and at a partner facility with the staff Reproductive Endocrinologist (patients are typically responsible out-of-pocket for the civilian lab/embryology portion, though overall costs are substantially lower than private-sector care).

### 2. What TRICARE *Does* Cover
While non-coital conception procedures like IVF are excluded, TRICARE **does cover** medically necessary diagnostic testing and treatments to correct underlying physical causes of infertility (when used in conjunction with natural conception). This includes:
* Hormone evaluations and blood work
* Semen analysis and sperm function tests
* Chromosomal, immunologic, and imaging studies (such as an HSG to check for blocked fallopian tubes)
* Bacteriologic investigations
* Surgeries or medical treatments to correct physical conditions (e.g., endometriosis, fibroids, or male factor issues)

### 3. Exception for Severely Ill or Injured Service Members
There is one major exception where TRICARE covers IVF and other ART services through the **Supplemental Health Care Program (SHCP)**:
* If the active duty service member sustained a serious or severe illness or injury (Category II or III) while on active duty that resulted in the loss of their natural procreative ability, ART services (including IVF, IUI, and gamete retrieval/storage) may be covered.

* **20 years of overlap:** There was at least a 20-year overlap between your marriage and the Marine's creditable military service.

Para inscribir a tu hijo(a) en la guardería (Child Care) en **Camp Pendleton**, el proceso se realiza principalmente en línea a través del portal oficial del Departamento de Defensa, con el apoyo de la oficina local de **Resource & Referral (Recursos y Referencias)** de MCCS.

### 1. Inscripción en línea (Paso principal)
Todas las solicitudes para los programas de cuidado infantil en Camp Pendleton se gestionan a través de **MilitaryChildCare.com**:
* **Crea una cuenta:** Ingresa a **MilitaryChildCare.com** y crea un perfil familiar.
* **Envía tu solicitud:** Busca las opciones disponibles en Camp Pendleton según la edad de tu hijo(a) y envía tu solicitud para ingresar a la lista de espera.
* **Asignación de espacios:** Los lugares se asignan según las prioridades del Departamento de Defensa (DoD) y la fecha de solicitud. Recibirás una notificación por correo electrónico cuando haya un espacio disponible.
* **Documentación necesaria:** Una vez que se te ofrezca un espacio, deberás presentar el registro de vacunación actualizado de tu hijo(a) y comprobantes de ingresos para calcular la tarifa (basada en el ingreso familiar total).

---

### 2. Oficina de Recursos y Referencias (Resource & Referral)
Si necesitas ayuda con el registro, orientación sobre tarifas o información sobre disponibilidad dentro y fuera de la base, puedes acudir o comunicarte directamente con la oficina de **Child and Youth Programs (CYP) Resource & Referral**:

* **Dirección:** Edificio (Bldg) 13150, #112 (entre 14th Street y C Street), Camp Pendleton, CA 92055
* **Horario de atención:** Lunes a viernes, de 7:30 a.m. a 4:30 p.m. (Cerrado sábados, domingos y días festivos)
* **Teléfono:** (760) 725-9723
* **Correo electrónico:** `resourcesreferralscp@usmc-mccs.org` o `mccspendleton.resourcereferral@usmc-mccs.org` *(Si las líneas telefónicas se encuentran ocupadas o fuera de servicio temporalmente, se recomienda contactar por correo electrónico o acudir en persona).*

---

### 3. Programas de cuidado infantil disponibles en Camp Pendleton
* **Child Development Centers (CDC):** Centros de desarrollo infantil para niños de **6 semanas a 5 años**. Camp Pendleton cuenta con centros ubicados en las áreas de Mainside (Courteau, De Luz, San Luis Rey), Main Gate (Stuart Mesa, Browne) y San Onofre.
* **Family Child Care (FCC):** Cuidado infantil en hogares certificados dentro de la base para niños de **6 semanas a 12 años**. Ofrece grupos más pequeños y mayor flexibilidad de horarios.
* **School Age Care (SAC):** Cuidado antes y después de la escuela, así como campamentos de vacaciones, para niños de **5 a 12 años** (kínder a 6.º grado).

### Elegibilidad
Los servicios están disponibles para hijos dependientes de personal militar en servicio activo, empleados civiles del DoD, reservistas en servicio activo o entrenamiento, y contratistas del DoD asignados a Camp Pendleton.

turns.user: My husband's unit deploys from Pendleton on Nov 14 to the Middle East. What support is there for spouses during deployment?
turns.agent:
Camp Pendleton offers several dedicated programs, support groups, and unit-level resources through Marine Corps Community Services (MCCS) to support you before and throughout your husband's deployment.

### 1. Weekly Deployment Support Group
You can start attending Camp Pendleton’s weekly support group right away—it is open to spouses whose Marines are either currently deployed or scheduled to deploy.
* **What it offers:** A welcoming space to build community with other spouses, receive emotional support, and share deployment-related resources. Children ages five and under are welcome to attend with you.
* **When:** Every Thursday from 9:00 AM – 10:00 AM
* **Location:** Community Counseling Center, Building 130193T, Camp Pendleton
* **Contact:** (760) 725-3884

---

### 2. Readiness & Deployment Support & Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB)
MCFTB and Readiness & Deployment Support Trainers offer workshops and resources tailored to every stage of the deployment cycle:
* **Pre-Deployment & Family Care Plans:** Briefings and workshops covering financial planning, powers of attorney, TRICARE, emergency communication, and setting up a Family Care Plan. If you need a personalized appointment before November 14, you can contact MCFTB directly.
* **Mid-Deployment Success Workshop:** Designed specifically for spouses and significant others at home, offering goal-setting tools, ideas for activities, local resources, and networking with other spouses.
* **Support for Children (Mid-Deployment Kids & Warrior Kids):** Workshops for children to help them process emotions around deployment and stay connected with their deployed parent.
* **Return & Reunion Workshops:** Held 14 to 30 days prior to the unit's return to help you prepare for homecoming, communication, and reintegration.
* **L.I.N.K.S. (Lifestyle, Insights, Networking, Knowledge, and Skills):** Spousal workshops that help you navigate base resources and connect with fellow Marine spouses.

**Contact & Location Details:**
* **Mainside Location:** Building 13150, Camp Pendleton
* **MCFTB West Location:** Building 202860, Camp Pendleton
* **Hours:** Monday – Friday, 7:00 AM – 4:30 PM
* **Phone:** Readiness & Deployment Support at (760) 763-1337 | Class Registration & Main MCFTB Line at (760) 725-9052 | MCFTB West at (760) 429-8363

---

### 3. Your Unit's Deployment Readiness Coordinator (DRC)
Every unit at Camp Pendleton has a dedicated **Deployment Readiness Coordinator (DRC)** (or military Uniform Readiness Coordinator, **URC**) who runs the Unit, Personal and Family Readiness Program (UPFRP).
* **What they do:** Serve as your primary link for official command updates while your husband is in the Middle East, coordinate unit family events, and provide direct resource referrals.
* **Next Step Before Nov 14:** Ask your husband for his unit DRC’s contact information to ensure you are added to the unit's official family readiness email distribution list.
* **How to Find Your DRC:** If you aren't sure who your unit's DRC is, you can call the **Camp Pendleton Family Readiness Program Office** at **(760) 763-1846** (Building 13150, Room 217A; Mon–Fri, 7:30 AM – 4:00 PM) or call Camp Pendleton Directory Assistance at **(760) 725-4111** and ask for your husband's unit DRC.

---

### 4. Confidential Counseling & Emotional Support
If you ever want one-on-one support for stress management or adjusting to the deployment, free confidential counseling is available on base:
* **Community Counseling Center (CCC):** Equips Marines and spouses with individual and family counseling.
  * **Location:** Building 130193T (Mainside) and Building 520512 (SOI area)
  * **Hours (Mainside):** Monday – Friday, 7:30 AM – 5:00 PM (Walk-in hours: Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM)
  * **Phone:** (760) 763-3222
* **Military & Family Life Counselors (MFLCs):** Provide confidential, non-medical counseling to help you navigate deployment stress. You can connect with them through the Marine & Family Programs office at Building 13150.

---

turns.agent:
Welcome to MCB Camp Lejeune! Finding childcare, a gym, and weekend activities is easy with the programs and facilities available on base.

---

### 1. Childcare for Your 2-Year-Old
MCCS Child and Youth Programs (CYP) offer care for children ages 6 weeks to 12 years through on-base **Child Development Centers (CDCs)** and certified in-home **Family Child Care (FCC)** providers. 
* **Services Offered:** Full-time care, hourly care, and special events care. Fees are based on total family income.
* **How to Request Care:** Start by submitting a request online at **MilitaryChildCare.com**. Because CDCs often have a waitlist, the CYP Resource and Referral office manages placements and can also help connect you with Family Child Care options.
* **CYP Resource & Referral Office:**
  * **Location:** Bldg. TT-113 (Tarawa Terrace II) or TT 2455H Iwo Jima Blvd, Camp Lejeune
  * **Hours:** Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM (Closed weekends and federal holidays)
  * **Phone:** (910) 450-0553 / 0554 / 0555
* **Documents Needed for Registration:** Your child’s immunization (shot) records, a health assessment/physical exam form, the sponsor's current LES/pay stub, and a Family Care Plan (if single or dual active duty).

---

### 2. Gyms & Fitness Centers
Camp Lejeune has several fitness centers across the installation that are free for authorized DoD ID cardholders. 

If you want to work out before your childcare is set up, **Wallace Creek Fitness Center** is a great first stop because it features a **Parent-View Fitness Zone**:
* **Wallace Creek Fitness Center**
  * **Parent-View Fitness Zone:** An enclosed area (maximum capacity of 5 children) designed to let parents work out while keeping their children directly within sight. *(Note: This is not a drop-off childcare service; parents must directly supervise their children at all times).*
  * **Amenities:** Strength and cardio equipment, functional training area, indoor pool, indoor climbing wall, group exercise classes, sauna, and smoothie bar.
  * **Location:** Bldg. WC1 Birch St., Camp Lejeune
  * **Hours:** Monday – Friday: 4:00 AM – 11:00 PM | Saturday & Sunday: 8:00 AM – 11:00 PM
  * **Phone:** (910) 450-7649

**Other Popular Base Fitness Centers (24/7 access available for Active-Duty personnel):**
* **French Creek Fitness Center:** Bldg. FC332 (off McHugh Blvd. & Gonzalez) | Staffed Mon–Fri 5:00 AM – 8:00 PM, Sat 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM, Sun 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM | (910) 451-5430
* **Courthouse Bay Fitness Center:** Bldg. BB2 (off Horn Rd.) | Staffed Mon–Thu 5:00 AM – 8:00 PM, Fri 5:00 AM – 7:00 PM, Sat 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM, Sun 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM | (910) 440-7447
* **MCAS New River Fitness Center:** Bldg. AS-4400 Douglass Rd. | Open Mon–Fri 4:00 AM – 10:00 PM, Sat & Sun 10:00 AM – 5:30 PM | (910) 449-4961

---

### 3. Fun for the Weekend
Several family-friendly options on base are perfect for exploring your new home this weekend:

* **Hit the Lanes at Bonnyman Bowling Center:**
  * Offers open bowling, bumpers for little ones, a snack bar/grill, and weekend specials.
  * **Weekend Specials:** Saturday afternoon special from 1:00 PM – 4:00 PM ($10/person for 2 games including shoe rental), and Glow Bowling on Friday & Saturday nights from 9:00 PM – Midnight.
  * **Phone:** (910) 451-5121
* **Relax at Onslow Beach:**
  * Camp Lejeune’s on-base beach is a great spot to walk along the water, picnic, or let your toddler play in the sand. There is also an on-site Marine Mart for snacks and essentials.
* **Get Outdoors at Gottschalk Marina & Base Ponds:**
  * Located on base, Gottschalk Marina offers kayak, canoe, paddleboard, and boat rentals, as well as scenic waterfront views. 
  * **Phone:** (910) 451-8307
* **Rent Gear for Home or the Park:**
  * If you want to have a weekend cookout or play yard games, **Recreation Equipment Issue** (Bldg. 1100 West Rd., (910) 451-1368) and the **MCAS New River Marina** rent out outdoor games, inflatables, grills, and bikes. *(Note: Camp Lejeune Equipment Issue is open Thursday and Friday from 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM and closed on weekends, so pick up gear on Friday if you want it for the weekend!)*

If you need directions to a specific facility or want information on programs like New Parent Support or Youth Sports, just let me know!
